attempts.hypothesis: This 64 kg biped's knee can only hold about 1.5× body weight, so I'm chasing a long-legged, lightly-compressed springy gait driven by a leg-length/leg-angle CPG with torso PD, an automatic actuator-sign probe at startup, and a full-covariance CEM search over 20 gait parameters.

This 64 kg biped ran at ~1.1 m/s before slowly sinking and falling at 13 s; I'm adding explicit torso-height feedback to prevent that drift, widening the frequency range to 3.5 Hz, seeding the search with 10 diverse speed-regime probes spanning walk→fast-run, and using a full-covariance CEM with res

This 64 kg biped's attempt-1 gait (14 m) died from slow height drift, so I'm keeping its leg-length/leg-angle CPG but adding integral height regulation, slope-adaptive lean, terrain-aware swing clearance, contact-gated force feedforward, and a seeded full-covariance CEM with pattern-search polish.

A 64 kg biped can only hold a foot within ±0.32 m of its hip in stance before its 195 N·m hips saturate and it pitches over, so I'm replacing the open-loop leg sweep with a world-fixed foot-hold stance servo (velocity-integrated foot anchor) plus terrain-following swing IK, adaptive stride frequency

After attempts 2-4 added complexity and got worse, I'm returning to the clean CPG + IK structure that worked in attempt 1 but with terrain-aware swing clearance for unseen hurdles, careful gravity feedforward, and a seed+CEM+coordinate-descent search that emphasizes survival time over raw speed.

This 64 kg biped topples when driven fast, so I'm simplifying to a clean leg-length/leg-angle CPG with IK, strong torso PD, velocity-dependent foot placement, terrain-aware swing clearance, and contact-synced phase—searched by seeded full-covariance CEM + coordinate descent over 14 parameters.

This biped's torso PD fights the natural forward lean of running, saturating the hip motors and starving gravity compensation until it tips over; I'm aligning the lean target with the running posture via negative velocity-dependent lean, prioritizing gravity in torque allocation, adding height/lean

Attempt 6's clean CPG+IK gait (10.9 m, 2nd best) is my foundation; I'm replacing the hardcoded velocity-lean with a searched coefficient, adding spring compression, and scoring survival time heavily in a diverse-regime-seeded full-covariance CEM to find the speed-stability sweet spot that survives t
I believe this creature needs a contact-aware alternating gait with torso correction, so I’m evolving its cadence and feedback gains while retaining a built-in terrain-clearance reflex.

I believe the first gait’s soft contact correction let its phases drift while the torso leaned back, so I’m making foot events realign the alternating gait more decisively and tuning support and terrain clearance together.
The proven gait is stable but slow, so I’m preserving its contact-locked controller while widening the cadence search and concentrating trials around that working solution.
I believe the contact-locked gait from the best 20-second run is a reliable base, so I’m preserving it while refining nearby parameters and favoring trials that finish.

I believe the late fall came from favoring a fast 10-second gait without enough margin, so I’m preserving the known 20-second contact-locked base and making the search conservative around it while retaining terrain clearance.

I believe the contact-locked gait is the safest core, so I’m preserving its rhythm while adding a memory-backed clearance reflex for abrupt hurdles and restricting learning to conservative refinements.
I believe the persistent sharp-rise lift was overreacting to ordinary terrain, so I’m restoring the previously reliable clearance gait and keeping its proven rhythm unless the baseline fails.
I believe the contact-locked gait is robust but slightly slow, so I’m searching small refinements and smoothly returning to its proven rhythm before the race’s second half.

I’m using a terrain-aware alternating gait controller with inverse-kinematics foot targets and joint PD control, then tuning its parameters by a bounded evolution strategy on the practice track, while biasing the final choice toward gaits that survive the full ten-second trial for better twenty-seco

I’m switching to a corrected balance-sign, feedback-driven joint-target gait: lean and velocity feedback now act through both foothold placement and direct hip torque, with conservative full-survival learning and terrain clearance for unseen hills/hurdles.

I’m keeping a feedback-driven virtual-leg gait but raising the body target, forcing realistic stride lengths, adding terrain-aware foot lift, and using a survival-weighted search with broad sign/phase seeds so the final gait is both faster and more durable.

I’m replacing the prior crouch-prone IK gait with a stabilized phase controller that keeps the body higher, starts from a planted double stance, adds strong knee-extension and contact recovery, and uses a survival-first evolutionary search with final perturbation checks for 20 s robustness.

I’m keeping the proven attempt-3 IK/phase controller as the fast gait core, adding velocity- and contact-aware stance locking with a terrain-obstacle lift, a conservative emergency stand transition, and a final learner that selects either a safe early-stop gait or a robust faster gait only when it b

I’m keeping the proven attempt-5 feedback gait as a safe baseline, adding optional propulsion/terrain-recovery terms initialized to zero, and using a local/CEM search that rewards full 10 s survival plus reliable phase-offset variants for better 20 s robustness.

I’m keeping the proven attempt-6/5 feedback gait as a safe fallback, while adding a more aggressive phase-IK runner with explicit swing clearance, toe-off push, direct torso-pitch torque, terrain anticipation, and late-race recovery; learning will only replace the fallback when it finds a clearly fa

I’m keeping the proven 4.4 m safe gait as a fixed fallback, and adding a terrain-triggered faster feedback gait with corrected pitch/velocity drive; the learner will only select it after full-survival validation, with conservative fallback and late-race stabilization.
I assume this is a bipedal gait that needs a phase-driven hip and knee rhythm with torso-angle balance feedback, so I'm tuning a compact 12-parameter CPG with a (1+λ) evolution strategy.
Attempt 1 fell at about 1.8 s with an open-loop clock, so I'm adding hip-driven phase entrainment, a hurdle-triggered knee lift, and a learner seeded with attempt 1's best gait.

Attempt 2's gait is a slow, balance-limited shuffle that falls forward once it speeds up, so I keep its policy unchanged and replace the learner with a seeded, normalised evolution strategy with restarts to search for faster gaits.

I believe the 3.8 m gait is a slow, balance-limited shuffle that falls forward when it speeds up, and the learner stalled on its seed, so I keep the attempt-3 policy and add one torso-lean setpoint parameter. I also replace the search with a seeded, mutation-based hill climber with restarts.

The gait is a slow, balance-limited shuffle that pitches forward near 3 m, so I'm keeping the attempt-4 policy with a wider knee lift for hurdles and replacing the search with a seeded, multi-start evolution strategy that restarts from diverse elite points.

The creature is a torque-limited, balance-limited shuffle near 0.33 m/s that pitches forward, and attempt 5's search was pinned against its parameter bounds (freq 3.2, hipAmp 0.9, hipMid 0.6), so I keep the proven policy, widen those ranges, and restart a seeded evolution strategy from attempt 5's b

The creature is a torque-limited shuffle that leans back and pitches forward near 3 m, so I keep the attempt-5/6 rhythm policy and run a local, bounded evolution strategy around the attempt-5 gait (6.68 m race) instead of the wide search that stalled.

Attempt 5's gait (6.68 m race, survived 20 s) is the best so far and attempts 6 and 7 regressed, so I keep its policy and run a small, low-variance local search from its parameters, returning a variant only if its trial score beats the seed.
